title: Arteta says conscious clear over time at Manchester City - CBS Sports
description: Newly committed to north London through 2030, the reigning champion brushed off questions regarding City's allege
body:
Newly committed to north London through 2030, the reigning champion brushed off questions regarding City's alleged rule breaches to focus on turning his side into the best in the world
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 9, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:00 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Arsenal have spent the last week talking themselves up as the coming force in world football, a club who believe they can be the best in the game for years to come and are prepared to say so repeatedly. Their manager, the only man in the Premier League with a winners' medal in his back pocket, has just put pen to paper on a contract that will extend his spell for a decade.And that was at best this week's B plot. Such is the gravitational pull of the Manchester City story. It is one that Mikel Arteta was always going to find himself drawn into. No manager can say they have experienced a Premier League warped by City quite like Arteta. As a player, he arrived at the Emirates Stadium a week after Samir Nasri had upped sticks for the Etihad. His coaching career began under Pep Guardiola, two of his three and a half years as an assistant falling within the period of the 114 breaches of Premier League rules. Then, of course, came the defining period of his career so far, the long and ultimately glorious battle against City for Premier League supremacy.There was plenty Arteta might have shared. Little he chose to. Ultimately, the nearest he got to a definitive statement on City was when asked, given his time at the club, whether his conscience was clear. "Yes," he said emphatically. That aside, the Spaniard was even more cagey on his former employers than he would be when asked about a high-profile injury. It was easy to see why Arteta might be reticent to speak for a club that has reserved the right to explore legal avenues against City once the Premier League's case has been concluded. He was no more candid, however, when it came to reflecting his own personal experience of that momentous day in Premier League history when the charges dropped."This has been going for various years," he said. "That process is still not finished. So it is very difficult to express how I feel, because it is not resolved. When it is resolved, I can talk with clarity and tell you exactly how I feel."
He will be held to that. Few came to London Colney expecting Arteta to expound on the City situation. Even if it weren't for his ties to the Etihad, it is just not his style to concern himself with many matters beyond his team, the crusade for more substitutes on the bench notwithstanding. The media room gravitas of reigning Premier League champion does not sit as easily on Arteta as it did, for instance, on Jurgen Klopp, let alone Arsene Wenger.Arteta was not the only one to play the many questions over City with a dead bat (this is a cricket reference for all you Americans out there). Andoni Iraola was similarly circumspect, ahead of his side's confrontation with City this weekend, though it was notable that Manchester United boss Michael Carrick, who might have had more Premier League winners' medals had it not been for City's rule-breaking, called for speed in concluding this process. That is a view shared by many other clubs in the Premier League, though on Friday's evidence Arteta was in no rush to resume questions over his past.His future seemed far more invigorating now that he is signed up to 2030. An extension to terms due to expire at the end of this season had long been expected; what was more notable was the way in which club and manager reached an agreement to prolong their partnership beyond the decade mark. Even when they end with one being the best-paid manager in the Premier League, few managers find themselves saying that they "loved" the negotiations after fresh terms have been agreed. Arteta is different.
He loved "the way we have analysed what we've done together and especially how we're going to take this club to be the best in the world for many years... You just have a sense how you feel about each other, how we do things, and I feel really lucky and having [co-chairs] Stan and Josh [Kroenke] in front of you and talking to them and expressing still what they want to do, how they want to do it, especially is just inspiring."That is not the first time since signing his new deal that Arteta has set expectations at a stratospheric level. Last season's Premier League title was, he said, just the beginning. Meanwhile, club chief executive Richard Garlick spoke about Arsenal "[dominating] football for the next number of years". That is a big ask for a team with one top-flight title to their name in 22 years, one that is still without that Champions League win that is a prerequisite of elite status. These are also the sort of lines that can come back to haunt a team, and yet Arteta is not afraid of setting the bar at the highest level."I don't think you have to hide it; the thing is that you have to earn it every single day. Your aspirations and your dreams are where they are. I think it's easier to get them [now]. If I said to you the one that I had when I arrived [as manager in 2019], probably you would say what are you talking about? 
"That was the ambition, that's the drive, and it's because we believe that we can do it, and then there will be many factors that would allow us or not to achieve it. Time will tell, but certainly that drive is there."And of course that opportunity to establish Arsenal as the leading lights in England and Europe is all the greater with their rivals facing what seems likely to be a cataclysmic set of sanctions. Not, of course, that Arteta would want to discuss it in those terms.

title: Breanna Stewart 'disappointed' refs refuted her account of timeout call in Game 2 as WNBA opens investigation - CBS Sports
description: The case of the missing reset timeout is ongoing as the Liberty and Dream get ready for Game 3
body:
The case of the missing reset timeout is ongoing as the Liberty and Dream get ready for Game 3
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 9, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:21 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Controversy embroiled the Atlanta Dream's thrilling 101-98 overtime victory over the New York Liberty in Game 2 of their semifinal series after Breanna Stewart accused the officials of incorrectly telling the Liberty that they had no timeouts remaining on the final play of overtime. Crew chief Fatou Cissoko-Stephens denied Stewart's version of events in the pool report, stating that there was "no direct communication" between the officials and the Liberty. The WNBA has reportedly opened an investigation into the matter. Stewart spoke to reporters on Friday ahead of Game 3 and expressed her frustration with the situation."You want to have respect between players and refs, and players and the league, and all these things. In order to have respect, you need to build trust. And building trust comes from being honest," she said. "And putting me in a position to question my integrity is really disappointing. I know who I am and what I stand for and what I heard. That's that."Regardless of what exactly transpired, the Liberty are now down 2-0 to the Dream in the best-of-five matchup, and no team in WNBA history has ever come back from a 2-0 deficit. As the Liberty try to figure out a way to get back into this series in Game 3 at home on Friday, here's a closer look at the disputed end to Game 2. 
With 4.3 seconds remaining in the extra frame, Angel Reese hit two clutch free throws to push the Dream's lead to three points. The Liberty had the ball and a reset timeout, however, and had sent the game to overtime with a brilliant after-timeout play that freed up Marine Fauthoux for a 3-pointer. So they still had hope -- at least it seemed. The Liberty did not call a timeout and instead tried to throw a long pass to Marine Johannès near midcourt. The ball was tipped, and even though it somehow wound up in Stewart's hands, her heave at the buzzer was nowhere close. In the initial aftermath, it appeared that first-year head coach Chris DeMarco had made a major blunder. 
But during the postgame press conference, Stewart explained why the Liberty did not call a timeout. 
"This is not blaming the refs, but when I ask both refs if we have a reset timeout and they tell us 'no,' and then we leave the game with a reset timeout, it's pretty frustrating," Stewart said. "Like, yeah, OK, I kinda got a good look at the end, but would just love to have some clarity on that situation as well.""I asked [official] Kevin [Fahy], I said, 'do we have a reset timeout?' And he said, 'I'm gonna check at the table,'" Stewart added. "He looked to [official] Fatou [Cissoko-Stephens], and she said, 'no,' then [Fahy] told me 'no.' Who knows what would have happened at the end of the game, but we would have had hopefully a better shot."
"Yeah, same thing," DeMarco said, when asked for his perspective on the situation. "They just said we didn't have it. Yeah, multiple staff members. It is what it is. We gotta demand more, but it is what it is."
In the pool report, which did not happen until well after an hour after the final buzzer, Cissoko-Stephens confirmed that the Liberty had a reset timeout available and refuted Stewart's version of events. "Stewart was standing behind referee Fahy when he confirmed with his partner between Reese's pentalty free throws that New York did indeed have a reset timeout remaining," Cissoko-Stephens said. 
Here is what the WNBA rulebook says about timeouts in overtime:"In overtime periods, each team shall be allowed two (2) team timeouts. There is no restriction as to when a team must call its timeouts during any overtime period.""Each team is entitled to one Reset in the final two minutes of the fourth period and one Reset in the last two minutes of any overtime period."The Liberty used their first timeout in overtime with 4:05 remaining to challenge a foul called on Fauthoux, which was upheld. They used their second timeout with 21 seconds remaining to draw up a play for a potential go-ahead basket that was not successful. As Cissoko-Stephens confirmed, they did indeed have their reset timeout, and should have been able to use it with 4.3 seconds left. But as Stewart noted, it was not the officials' fault that the Liberty lost. Dream star Allisha Gray did not play due to a hand injury and Rhyne Howard shot 5 of 20. The Liberty were also up by three with less than two minutes to play in overtime and on their second-to-last possession, Sabrina Ionescu threw a ball into the fifth row. The Liberty had their chances, and even if they had used their reset timeout successfully, would have only been able to force a second overtime. 
At the same time, if Stewart's version of events is accurate -- and despite the pool report, it's hard to believe she's lying given her reputation -- that is a massive blunder by the officials that absolutely cannot happen at that stage of a playoff game.

title: Eagles releasing veteran QB Andy Dalton, still unsettled at QB2 behind Jalen Hurts - CBS Sports
description: Dalton will begin the process of finding a new team

        The Philadelphia Eagles have made a surprise personnel move as they prepare for Sunday's game against the Jaguars in London. The team has released veteran quarterback Andy Dalton, according to multiple reports. Dalton, who will turn 39 later this month, was intercepted in his only pass attempt this season. It occurred in the end zone during the first half of Philadelphia's eventual Week 3 loss to the Chicago Bears when Jalen Hurts temporarily left the game after getting hit by Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson. 
Dalton's spot on the Eagles' depth chart will be replaced by Tanner McKee and rookie Cole Payton. McKee, a 2023 sixth-round pick, has made one start in the last two years. He has five career touchdown passes and one interception and has completed 61.4% of his passes. Payton, a fifth-round pick in this year's draft, has yet to play in a regular-season game.While the Eagles adjust their quarterback room, Dalton will begin his search for a new team. A three-time Pro Bowler, Dalton spent his first nine NFL seasons with the Bengals, with whom he helped lead to the playoffs five straight seasons from 2011-16. He has also spent time with the Saints, Bears and Panthers. 
In his career, Dalton has thrown for 39,793 yards, 254 touchdowns, and 152 interceptions. He has completed 62.6% of his passes. Where will Dalton end up next? Here are a few possible landing spots. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    VikingsMinnesota could use another backup quarterback after it traded JJ McCarthy to the Giants. In Dalton, the Vikings would have two veteran quarterbacks behind Kyler Murray, alongside Carson Wentz. Wentz played well earlier this season after Murray sustained an injury. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Giants Speaking of the Giants, they could also use a veteran quarterback after losing Jaxson Dart to a season-ending injury. Jameis Winston is coming off his best game as a Giant, but it's safe to say that the Giants would still benefit from having another quarterback in the room. However, after acquiring JJ McCarthy, it's unlikely they're willing to make another move.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Saints This is a situation where Dalton could serve as a mentor for Tyler Shough, whose season so far has had its share of ups and downs. At this point, Shough does not have a mentor in the quarterback room. His current backup is Spencer Rattler, who is a year younger than he is. Dalton could be a valuable sounding board for a young room looking for some guidance.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Dolphins Like New Orleans, Dalton could serve as a mentor in Miami for Malik Willis, who is currently entrenched in his first season as a full-time starter. Willis' current backup, Kyle McCord, is also in his first year with the Dolphins and has yet to play in an NFL regular-season game. But the question remains whether the tanking Dolphins would go after a quarterback now or get their pick during the 2027 NFL Draft. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    TitansAnother team where Dalton could help a young quarterback find his footing. Cam Ward, the No. 1 overall pick in the 2025 NFL draft, is still growing as a starting quarterback. It's safe to assume that a player with Dalton's experience would help him with his continued development.

        USC wide receiver Terrell Anderson will undergo season-ending surgery, according to CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz. Anderson was a huge pick-up for the Trojans in the transfer portal, but his season is over after just three games and two receptions for 50 yards.A four-star recruit coming out of high school, Anderson spent the first two seasons of his college career at NC State, where he broke out as a sophomore in 2025. Last fall, Anderson totaled 39 receptions for 629 yards and five touchdowns.When Anderson entered the portal, there was plenty of interest in him, given his unique combination of size and skill. He was ranked as the No. 10 overall transfer, according to 247Sports. When the Trojans signed Anderson, he was viewed as a potential superstar with Jayden Maiava throwing him the football.
Unfortunately for Maiava and the Trojans, the injury has impacted Anderson throughout the season. He missed the season-opener against Fresno State, and he played only sparingly in the last three games. Anderson recorded two receptions for 50 yards in a loss to Oregon, but that's the only time he appeared on the stat sheet outside of punt returns.
With Anderson on the shelf for the remainder of the season, USC will need production from other players in the passing game, but the receiver room has been banged up in the early going.Injury bug biting USC pass-catchersAnderson isn't the only key receiver who has dealt with injuries in Los Angeles. Freshman wideout Trent Mosley got off to a terrific start with 255 yards and four touchdowns in three games. However, he's been sidelined for the last two games after suffering a knee injury.Freshman tight end Mark Bowman, the No. 42 overall player in the 2026 signing class, is also dealing with an injury after missing the Washington game last week. Bowman has 21 catches for 204 yards and two touchdowns through four games.
Mosley and Bowman are both listed as questionable for Saturday night's road game against Penn State.With Anderson, Mosley and Bowman all less than 100 percent, receivers Zach Williams and Kayden Dixon-Wyatt will be asked to pick up some of the slack. Williams and Dixon-Wyatt currently lead the team in receiving, and they'll get plenty of targets in Happy Valley.Sophomore wideout Tanook Hines will also factor into the equation, and he made an exceptional touchdown catch against the Huskies last weekend. If Hines continues to elevate his game, that would make the loss of Anderson -- and the rest of the offensive injuries -- easier to overcome.

title: Dream, Angel Reese sweep Liberty as Atlanta reaches first WNBA Finals since 2013 - CBS Sports
description: Atlanta, powered by Reese and Jordin Canada, pulled off the sweep with a two-point win on the road
body:
Atlanta, powered by Reese and Jordin Canada, pulled off the sweep with a two-point win on the road
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 9, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:22 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Atlanta Dream advanced to the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2013 in thrilling fashion with an 85-83 victory over the New York Liberty in Game 3 of their semifinal series. After a three-game sweep of the Liberty, the Dream will face either the Golden State Valkyries or Las Vegas Aces in the Finals, which will begin on Oct. 17. The Dream jumped in front early in an extremely physical contest that nearly got out of hand on multiple occasions as the officials let just about everything go. Notably, Angel Reese got in Sabrina Ionescu's face after the Liberty guard delivered a hard foul to Isobel Borlase as payback for what she thought should have been a foul on Borlase. And later, both Reese and Jonquel Jones were hit with technicals after a dust-up under the basket. Early in the second half, the Dream pushed their lead up to 12, but the Liberty immediately responded and took a lead of their own into the fourth. When Ionescu hit a 3-pointer 30 seconds into the final frame to push the Liberty's lead to five, it seemed they might pull away. Instead, it became a back-and-forth affair down the stretch. After Jordin Canada hit a circus shot to give the Dream a four-point advantage with just over a minute to play, Jones responded to cut the deficit to two. The Liberty then got a few stops and had multiple chances to tie the game. One ended with a Ionescu turnover -- she had a crucial turnover at the end of Game 2 as well -- and the other ended with a miss by Breanna Stewart. 
DeWanna Bonner, who stepped up yet again in this postseason with 13 points and 13 rebounds, then iced the game at the free throw line. Canada, who was tremendous all series, finished with 19 points, 11 assists and no turnovers, while Reese 22 points and nine rebounds. Jones was excellent for the Liberty in defeat with 26 points, 14 rebounds and three blocks, while Stewart added 26 points of her own. 
The Dream have been to the Finals three times, but have been swept on every occasion. They'll look to change that trend this time, and potentially win the first title in franchise history.

        The comparisons between Bob Chesney and Curt Cignetti are numerous. Both worked their way up as journeymen from the lower levels of the sport, stacking double-digit-win teams and even placing players in the NFL. For Chesney, his path took him from Division III Salve Regina to Division II Assumption to FCS Holy Cross. Conference championships followed at each stop.Both coached at James Madison, where they led the Dukes to conference championships and, for Chesney, a spot in the 12-team playoff. Both moved to down-on-their-luck Big Ten basketball schools and brought in players they were familiar with to help revamp their rosters. Thirteen JMU players followed Cignetti to Bloomington, and seven remained on the national title roster. UCLA has a dozen former Dukes on its roster, and roughly half are significant contributors.A key difference in roster build is the perceived level of talent. Whereas Indiana ranked 72nd in the 247Sports Talent Composite coming into last season, UCLA is 24th in 2026, largely due to the retention of key players, notably five-star Nico Iamaleava.At Indiana, Cignetti has capped one of the great turnaround stories in the sport's history with a national title. In Chesney's case, he hopes his import will also produce program-changing results. It's certainly too early to tell, but how are these Bruins built? CBS Sports goes inside the roster to break it down.
Note: If the player is a transfer, the star rating is his 247Sports transfer rating, not his high school rating. "(2025)" denotes a player in UCLA's 2025 transfer class, and therefore inherited by Chesney.QuarterbackNico Iamaleava — Sr. | Transfer from Tennessee | ★★★★★ (2025)According to Iamaleava, it only took one meeting to convince him that staying at UCLA and close to home was the right decision. Chesney has been clear that retaining him was key in bridging the culture past the dysfunction of the 2025 season. So far, his legs have been the bigger asset than his arm, but his leadership has been key.Running BackWayne Knight — 5th Yr. | Transfer from James Madison | ★★★Anthony Woods — 5th Yr. | Transfer from Utah | ★★★ (2025)
The team's current star and most productive offensive player had to be talked into coming back to a James Madison team he'd been estranged from when Chesney arrived in Harrisonburg. He fielded offers from other schools last offseason but decided to follow Chesney to LA in the portal.Four games into the season, he paces one of the country's best rushing attacks with a stunning 9.08 yards per carry. He is simply on a tear and currently has more rushing touchdowns than 30 Power Four teams."I know this guy wins," Knight said about Chesney to the school's website. "He wants to talk to his players. He wants to get to know you and know your journey and just know what kind of person you are. So, you can not only be a better player for him, but a better man after it's all said and done."
Wide ReceiverPlayerClassTransfer FromRatingBrian Rowe Jr.So.South Carolina★★★Landon EllisSr.James Madison★★★Semaj MorganSr.Michigan★★★UCLA's passing game has yet to truly get going (Morgan leads in receptions with 14 so far this season), but it hasn't had to, considering how well the Bruins have controlled games on the ground.Tight EndPlayerClassTransfer FromRatingBrayden Loftin5th Yr.Kansas State★★★Harry Lodge5th Yr.Wake Forest★★★In a passing game that isn't prolific, UCLA's tight ends are most often used as extra run blockers.Offensive LinePlayerClassTransfer FromRatingJordan Davis5th Yr.South Alabama★★★Eugene BrooksJr.Oklahoma★★★ (2025)Riley RobellSr.James Madison★★★Carter Sweazie5th Yr.James Madison★★★Hall Schmidt5th Yr.Boise State★★★Jensen SomervilleJr.—★★★The most intriguing part of Chesney's James Madison import is that it includes two interior offensive linemen in Sweazie and Robell. The interior is where height and length are a bit less of a concern than at tackle, especially regarding Sweazie, who is a 6-foot-1 guard. But they plow the road for one of the nation's most efficient run games, and they're part of a unit that includes other Group of Six players identified by UCLA's personnel staff as contributors.

Rotation can keep a unit fresh, as it does for the Bruins, as does having huge leads in most of the games they've played so far this season. title: How is Mike Norvell still employed? Buyout, leadership uncertainty keeping hot seat coach at FSU - CBS Sports
description: Norvell's seat hasn't gotten any cooler, but Florida State has been hesitant to make a move
body:
Norvell's seat hasn't gotten any cooler, but Florida State has been hesitant to make a move

    10:51 pm ET

        Mike Norvell entered the 2026 season on the hottest seat in college football, and it certainly hasn't gotten any cooler.The temperature of Norvell's seat only got warmer on Friday night as Florida State blew an early 14-0 lead in a 44-20 loss to Louisville. The Seminoles were knocking on the door of a 21-0 advantage when they failed to convert on fourth-and-goal.On the very next play from scrimmage, Cardinals' running back Isaac Brown took a handoff 97 yards to the house, and Florida State never had control of the game again. Brown would later add a 68-yard rushing score as he finished the night with 235 yards on the ground.
Blowing a 14-point lead only to lose by 14-plus points hasn't been a common occurrence for the Seminoles throughout their history, but it's become a habit this season.
Coming into the year, that hadn't happened once in 385 games over the last 30 years. It's now happened twice in the last four weeks, with Florida State also blowing a 21-6 lead on the road against Alabama.Despite more troubling results, Florida State has yet to make a coaching change. Naturally, that leads one to wonder whether the school will make a move at all this season, and even if it does, when?The reality is that Norvell has a couple of factors working in his favor, including his massive buyout and an athletic department in flux.
Norvell's prohibitive buyoutIf Florida State is going to fire Norvell, it'll have to pay him a fortune in order to do so. Norvell's buyout currently sits at $46.7 million, which is a lot of money for any program, but especially for one that hasn't kept up with the times as far as NIL Is concerned.According to our own Chris Hummer and John Talty, the Seminoles are paying just north of $20 million for their 2026 roster, which puts them in the middle of the pack in the ACC and well behind serious championship contenders around the country.Would Florida State be willing to shell out double what it's currently paying for the football roster just to fire Norvell? That $46.7 million price tag doesn't even factor in buyouts for assistants or the cost of hiring another coach and bringing in his staff.
Because of that financial bind, there is a sense that Norvell could keep his job with a decent finish. As much as Friday night's loss to Louisville hurt, last week's thrashing of Virginia helped Norvell's job security.Next weekend's game against Miami may be a lost cause, but the Seminoles have winnable games against Clemson, Boston College, Pittsburgh and NC State after that. Norvell could save himself with a strong run of form over that stretch.Uncertainty in the athletic departmentQuestions about how Florida State funds its athletic programs have prompted changes at the administrative level. The school fired athletic director Michael Alford back in September, and Bruce Warwick is serving as interim athletic director while the university re-evaluates its operations in the modern landscape.
According to CBS Sports' Richard Johnson, Florida State is looking to abandon the old ways of doing business in college sports. The Seminoles are keeping close tabs on which way the realignment winds are blowing as they consider what life might be like outside the ACC.The days of the old-school athletic director are gone, and Florida State has found that out the hard way. The next athletic director will be tasked with finding new and innovative ways to maximize revenue in what has become a financial arms race.Because of all that uncertainty, Norvell may be safe for the time being. There is no full-time athletic director above him in the chain of command -- and, in the big picture, Florida State is still trying to figure out exactly where it wants to go and how it wants to get there.

        Hurricanes Isaias has affected travel plans around the country, and that includes President Donald Trump. Originally, Trump planned to be in attendance when No. 2 Georgia faced No. 6 Alabama in Bryant-Denny Stadium on Saturday, but the Tuscaloosa Police Department told AL.com that he scrapped the trip due to the impending storm.Trump has attended several Alabama football games throughout his tenure, and he's friendly with legendary coach Nick Saban, who has expressed support for Trump as it pertains to the Protect College Sports Act.In 2018, Trump made the trip down to Atlanta for the College Playoff National Championship, which the Crimson Tide won due to overtime heroics from Tua Tagovailoa. The next year, in 2019, Trump was at Bryant-Denny Stadium for the shootout that was LSU vs. Alabama.While weather may have nixed this trip, Trump has gotten to watch a little college football in person this season. He was in Knoxville just two weeks ago when Texas triumphed over Tennessee, 20-17.
For the moment, Hurricanes Isaias isn't expected to change much about the game itself. Both teams are planning to play on Saturday night in Tuscaloosa as scheduled, but the SEC is monitoring the storm and the kickoff time could be altered slightly.The storm is expected to bring locally heavy rain, potential flooding, high winds and isolated tornadoes throughout the Southeast this weekend, although the exact path is still unknown.According to both coaches, the teams are preparing as normal for the game, since the weather is well outside of their control. Wet-ball drills and mental preparation are all that can be done for now.
"Depends on the level of weather you get, it would affect what happens," Alabama coach Kalen DeBoer said, according to 247Sports. "It's just -- that's not my area of expertise. I'm just getting our football team ready. It hasn't affected us much, other than we're doing wet ball drills and get wet ball involved in some of our team reps, just like we did last week at times, preparing for the rain a week ago. I'm not really involved in too much."

        The Philadelphia Eagles' (2-2) offense is officially in free fall. Philadelphia is coming off an epic meltdown home defeat against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 4 in which they blew a double-digit lead and went 0-12 in third-down conversion attempts. In the wake of that loss, Eagles six-time Pro Bowl right tackle Lane Johnson retired on Tuesday, and the team then traded two-time Pro Bowl offensive lineman Cam Jurgens to the Baltimore Ravens. That's on top of their CVS receipt-length injury list, which includes 2024 NFL Offensive Player of the Year running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), both being ruled out ahead of Week 5 against the Jacksonville Jaguars (3-1) in London.
That means Week 5 could look a lot like Week 4. Quarterback Jalen Hurts completed just 12 of his 27 throws for 93 yards while taking four sacks. That all added up to a career-low 3.0 yards per dropback. Since Week 3, Hurts is averaging an NFL-worst 4.7 yards per pass attempt after ranking 11th best in the league in that same metric with a 7.5 yards per pass average through the first two weeks of the season. The good news for the Eagles is that even with a loss in Week 5, the NFC East will likely remain up for grabs. The New York Giants are 3-1, but their ceiling is capped by the season-ending knee injury to quarterback Jaxson Dart. Fill-in Jameis Winston ranks dead last in the NFL in completion percentage at 55.1% this season. The Giants are also without three-time Pro Bowl edge rusher Brian Burns, their best pass rusher, whose 16.5 sacks ranked second in the league in 2025, for the rest of the year after he tore his ACL and meniscus. The Washington Commanders are 1-3, and quarterback Jayden Daniels is once again dealing with an elbow injury. 
It will be interesting to see how head coach Nick Sirianni and offensive coordinator Sean Mannion adjust to the absences of both their star playmakers, with the team facing a schematic clash early in the season.

description: The USWNT will be without center back Naomi Girma and defensive midfielder Sam Coffey for this month's friendlies
body:
The USWNT will be without center back Naomi Girma and defensive midfielder Sam Coffey for this month's friendlies against Spain, who will ultimately test the hosts' depth in defense
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 9, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:50 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        For a team with the explicit goal of winning the Women's World Cup, there is no test more perfect than a pair of friendlies against the last team to take home the title. To do it a month before World Cup qualifiers and eight months before the tournament itself makes for perfect timing. The U.S. women's national team remain as well-equipped as any to handle the challenges Spain will pose over the next week, starting with Saturday's friendly in the nation's capital, but make no mistake – the circumstances are not exactly perfect.The reigning Olympic gold medalists are still the attack-minded force they have always been, but they will be understaffed for their doubleheader against Spain, and in a key area of the pitch. Center back Naomi Girma and defensive midfielder Sam Coffey were ruled out of the games with injuries, leaving the USWNT particularly understaffed in defense. Claire Hutton will likely fill Coffey's role and may have done so anyway, such is the quality of the 20-year-old. Head coach Emma Hayes has an eclectic group to work with at center back, though: Tierna Davidson, Girma's presumed partner at the World Cup next year; Tara Rudd, who joined the fold after the U.S. team won gold at the 2024 Olympics; Kennedy Wesley, who has seven caps; and Kate Del Fava, a first-timer with the senior national team after years of experience in the NWSL."Can't do anything about that," Hayes said candidly on Friday, though she does not exactly feel down on her luck.How to watch USWNT vs. Spain, oddsDate: Saturday, Oct. 10 | Time: 2:30 p.m. ETLocation: Audi Field -- Washington, D.C.TV: TBS | Live stream: HBO MaxOdds: USWNT +260; Draw +250; Spain -110
"They're top players and I can put them in situations this week to create the exposures," she continued. "I think developing as a pairing is something that they're going to have to do, but I believe in them, and I watch their attention to detail. I think you got [Tierna], who, by nature, is a defender that can progress the ball up the pitch. Great covering defender, really good aerially. You got Kennedy, who steps to the play really well. I think they're actually a good complement to each other. I think they're very intelligent people, so they can solve really good tactical puzzles, and I've seen them do it all week, so I'm looking forward to seeing how they progress together."The 25-year-old Wesley is one of the late beneficiaries of Hayes' player pool expansion project following the Olympics but has been a focal point for the San Diego Wave, who remain in the hunt for the NWSL Shield thanks in large part to their league-leading defensive efforts. Her stock appears to on the rise and at a timely juncture in the USWNT's preparations for the World Cup, and Wesley seems to be soaking up every moment along the way."I think both Tierna, [Emily Fox], there are so many players that bring an ample amount of experience and it's been nothing so, so helpful to me, recognizing I can go to them with any question I have." Wesley said Thursday. "If I'm hesitant, they're always the first ones to kind of back me in my decisions, so it's been really awesome training with them the last few days and for the last few months, but I do think that their experience will help us propel in moments when we need it in the game. When we have long spells of defending, when the momentum might not be our way, I think those are players that I've relied on, the group can rely on in those really tough moments."
The group will perhaps be equally reliant on her on Saturday, Spain's impressive attack headlined by two-time Ballon d'Or-winning playmaker Alexia Putellas set to offer the USWNT's defense – understaffed or otherwise – their stiffest challenge yet. The U.S. team's defense has gone somewhat untested since the Olympics, with opponents averaging just seven shots per game and less than one expected goal along the way. The numbers are not all that different against teams ranked in FIFA's top 10, though Spain pose their own challenges."I think the first thing that comes to mind is that we're going to need to be really disciplined," Wesley said. "I think they're so dynamic in their movements, in their interchange when they have the ball, when they're in possession so it'll be really really important for us to be disciplined, not get pulled out of position so that we can kind of dispute their attack but I also think working form the back to front, it'll be really important we're really front-footed and pressing high on the field, not allowing them space and time because I think that's what they're the most successful so I think between the discipline and the front-footedness, I think those are really important."Chemistry questions are not reserved solely for the back line, even if they will be in focus as Spain attempt to impose their possession-oriented, attack-minded style. Hayes has spent the post-Olympic period expanding the player pool, tinkering with her lineups over the course of 30 games as she builds experience and depth in each area of the pitch. In both friendlies against Spain, though, she boasted that the lineups will be fairly similar and that the time for experimentation is essentially over. Though it is hard to envision a first-choice version of the USWNT without Girma in the lineup if she's available, Hayes might answer questions about who's leading the race for starting roles in attack at the World Cup.
Many of her mainstays are available, including the Triple Espresso – Trinity Rodman, Sophia Wilson and Mallory Swanson – though she is hardly limited in that department. Regulars including Alyssa Thompson, Emma Sears and Michelle Cooper are all amongst the bunch, and that group alone is a stark reminder that the U.S. team's historic attacking might is going nowhere."I think the cool part about the front line is that we all have chemistry in different ways," Wilson said. "I think we all can work together and kind of get the same product, and it doesn't really matter who's out there. I think we trust everyone to step up when their name is called. I think defensively, we really pride ourselves on being a high-pressing team and a team that wants to press and press with speed because I think we can create chances that way, and I think we have the players to do that, so just following that and knowing that's one of our strengths and I think it will be a strength against Spain."There are some newcomers in the group; their abilities to break into the core player pool still unclear. Trinity Byars and Pietra Tordin are amongst those who could earn their first cap, while Ashley Sanchez marks an impressive return to the national team around two years after she was last in the group. It is a well-earned return to the fold for Sanchez, who tagged along for the 2023 World Cup but has not been much of a fixture with the USWNT since. She leads the NWSL with 20 goals and is likely in the midst of an MVP-caliber season and, like Wesley, is also charting an upward trajectory at the right time.
"I think it's really cool and I'm obviously really proud of her," Rodman, her longtime teammate at the Washington Spirit before Sanchez's trade to the Courage in 2024, said. "I think through her career, she's been through a lot- ups and downs of coming into the national team, not starting, getting traded, and just so many things that I think that she's overcome, and even just playing in the midfield and now being the top goalscorer on the wing, I think, is really impressive, and I'm just really happy for her, and I do think this is her time, and I'm very excited to be able to share the field with her, and I think she deserves it. To be able to kind of play a lot of her career as a midfielder and to now thrive up top, I think, brings just another piece to the game and can also bring another type of forward to this lineup as well, which I think is really good for us."The fact that the USWNT enters their doubleheader against Spain with unanswered questions is intriguing in its own right; uncertainty rarely reassuring, no matter the circumstances. From the team's perch, though, it is all by design."Even [the World Cup] just being next year, I think we've already kind of got into that mindset, but obviously, we need to qualify," Wilson said. "But I think this team has been preparing for the World Cup since the day the Olympics ended. I think that's just the mindset, that everything we do in between these tournaments is just in preparation for the next."

Emma Hayes gets two cracks at the world's best as Ashley Sanchez returns in elite form and Trinity Rodman leads a dynamic attack

        This international break, soccer fans will be in for a treat as the number one and number two women's national teams face each other in Spain and the United States. During this camp, USWNT head coach Emma Hayes will get to see her squad face one of the top teams in the world as the road to the 2027 World Cup in Brazil continues. With players missing and depth concerns in defense, it's a good camp for Hayes to see what may need to change, and playing Spain twice allows time to tinker between games.Because of that, I took a look at some things to watch for during camp:Ashley Sanchez's role in a new positionOne doesn't tie the NWSL scoring record by accident, and no matter how you slice Ashley Sanchez's season with the N.C. Courage, it's quite impressive. But when peeling back how it's happening, that's when things get remarkable. For Sanchez's career, she has played as a striker or creative attacking midfielder, but in some of the best form of her career and earning the first national team call in two years, she's doing neither.
                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            Head coach Mak Lind has come in and positioned Sanchez as a strict left winger. Playing as a right-footed forward on the left side, she's been able to cut inside, flip the ball to her right foot, and next thing you know, the keeper is picking the ball out of the back of their net. Looking at her finishes, it's easy to see why she has been overperforming her xG of 13.98. But even if that's stripped away, only Sophia Wilson has a higher xG on the season, and that's quite good company to be in. The front three of the USWNT is something which felt more settled than other positions on the pitch, but when someone is performing at Sanchez's level, they can't be left out of the national team, and that's a good problem to have when creating competition for the World Cup.Trinity Rodman is a creative forceLooking at one of the ways that Sanchez may get the ball, Trinity Rodman is the heartbeat of the attack because a defender never knows what she'll do. Already dynamic on the ball going forward, Rodman has a strong balance of scoring and creativity, and she could etch her name in NWSL history. In the NWSL regular season, there has never been a player to collect 10 goals and 10 assists in a season, and with 11 goals and eight assists, Rodman could do it with three games remaining in the Washington Spirit's season. She's not alone in chasing that as Cloe Lacasse and Pietra Tordin are also tracking to that number for the Utah Royals and Portland Thorns, respectively. There are a few reasons why so many players are on pace for something that has never been done before, as games have been added to the league and the quality of forwards entering has risen by the day, but a defense also doesn't know where Rodman will pop up to make them pay.

                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            Operating fluidly on the wing, she's just as likely to attack the box from the left as she is the right, and it helps make Hayes' USWNT unpredictable, which is important when facing Spain. If the USWNT aren't at their best, this will be a long international break, and Rodman is one of the keys to unlocking Spain's defense, as no matter where the other forwards move, she can move to set them up or generate her own shot.Does wing back Alyssa Thompson move back into the attack?Someone who generally operates as a forward, Alyssa Thompson has also undergone a position shift this season at Chelsea, moving slightly deeper to operate as a wing back. She has still been able to get in the box from left back, scoring a goal for Chelsea on 13 shots, but how this shift impacts her usage will be something to watch during this camp. On the one hand, becoming more well-rounded defensively could give the USWNT another wrinkle to unlock, but it could also lead to shifts among the forward line depending on how Hayes wants to set the squad up.Attacking-wise, with Sanchez here, there is a chance that Thompson isn't the top forward to bring into the game, but Hayes also doesn't set up in a back three, which is where things get a little wonky. At 21, she is among the members of the squad with the highest ceiling, but ceilings don't always lead to immediate minutes when there are matches to win.
Who is the secondary creator in midfield?Without Croix Bethune and Olivia Moultrie, midfield is thinner than expected, but Hayes could be able to plug Mal Swanson in wherever she needs as versatility grows among the attack. Swanson may have only played in 12 games this season for the Chicago Stars but she's been back in the lineup and performing well."She can play as the 10, she can play as the seven, the nine, the 11," Hayes said at her pre-match press conference. "When I think of a midfielder, I think of Lindsay [Heaps] Lilly [Yohannes]. I think she definitely looks more like herself and has made good progress since Brazil. I've seen some things in training this week that show she's on the right path, and 10 months postpartum, I don't think her road was easy so I expected things to take a little more time and support, but I think she's really finding her feet."Name-dropping Heaps and Yohannes shouldn't come as a surprise, as they'd be expected to take up the deeper roles in midfield, but who is ahead of them could be anyone's guess, as this is such a fluid team. That's a critical question to answer ahead of the World Cup too, as while some of the injured players could return by then, there is a need for depth in key positions.
